suites.framework: custom (tsx script driving the real Railway worker via submission_queue rows)
suites.last_known_status_claim: 2026-08-13 session: 50 real submission_queue rows across 3 disposable test orgs, monitored live against the real deployed Railway worker for the full 130-minute safety cap. Result: 0/50 items reached a terminal status before the cap -- explicitly NOT a hang or bug: worker/queue-processor.ts calls waitBetweenSubmissions() (a random 60-120s sleep) after every single item regardless of outcome, so a full 50-item drain needs 50-100+ minutes minimum even error-free; hitting the 130-min cap is the expected, documented result of this real rate limiter, not evidence of a defect. Zero errors/rate-limit/CAPTCHA/crash/memory issues observed. All disposable test data confirmed deleted afterward.

notes: This inventory was assembled from filesystem discovery + governance-doc cross-reference, not from freshly executing any suite. 'ran_to_completion' reflects whether existing repo evidence (a committed log, JSON result file, or dated governance-doc narrative with a concrete pass/fail count) demonstrates the suite was run and reached a final result -- not whether every test in it passed.

Several suites (unit-src, e2e-authed, e2e-public, e2e-critical-paths-others, smoke-vitest-api, smoke-playwright-*, smoke-platform-script) have zero discoverable evidence of ever completing a run in this repo -- flagged 'unknown' rather than assumed passing or failing.

visual-regression is the one suite with affirmative evidence it CANNOT have passed in its current committed state: no baseline snapshot directory exists on disk, and Playwright's toHaveScreenshot() fails (does not silently pass or auto-generate) against a missing baseline.

Two files literally named 'smoke' exist under different Playwright projects with different scope: tests/smoke.spec.ts ("public" project) and e2e/smoke.spec.ts ("critical-paths" project) -- do not conflate them.

tests/api, tests/lib, and tests/unit are directory names carried over from an earlier Jest-oriented layout, but no Jest dependency exists in package.json today -- all three are matched and run exclusively by vitest.config.ts's include pattern ("tests/**/*.test.ts") under vitest, per project convention documented across multiple STATE_OF_THE_BUILD.md sessions.
